mainTopic: Passing objects through a מקום פטור between domains, the water-channel dispute, and drawing water from a balcony over water on שבת
overview: This amud joins a sugya already in progress about moving objects between two domains by passing them through a small exempt spot (מקום פטור). The גמרא first says that רב דימי's ban on exchanging through such a spot applies only to Torah-level domains, not to רשויות דרבנן. It then challenges this with the משנה of a wall between two courtyards. On that משנה, רבי יוחנן rules that for a wall under four טפחים wide, each side may use it but may not exchange. The גמרא answers that this strict version of רבי יוחנן is זעירי's tradition, not רב דימי's. It then explains how זעירי reads the earlier water-channel ruling and defends that reading with the question of whether a כרמלית has 'holes'. רבינא offers a different reading, tied to the known dispute about לבוד. A new משנה follows about drawing water through a balcony over water on שבת, which requires a ten-טפח partition. The גמרא contrasts this with חנניא בן עקביא, whose leniency applied only at ים טבריא. It begins explaining his three leniencies for the people of טבריא, and the explanation of storing produce in pods continues on the next amud.

steps.title: Here the domains are only rabbinic
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא explains that רב דימי's leniency deals with domains whose separation is only דרבנן.
steps.simpleTranslation: Here we are dealing with domains that are only rabbinic.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers an earlier difficulty with רב דימי's ruling. It says his case involves domains that are separated only by rabbinic law.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Moving an object from רשות היחיד to a כרמלית is forbidden only מדרבנן. Since the ban itself is rabbinic, the חכמים did not forbid passing the object through a מקום פטור on the way. So רב דימי's restriction ('as long as they do not exchange') applies only to Torah-level domains, not to the rabbinic domains in this case.

keyTerms.meaning: domains (areas with their own שבת carrying status)
by rabbinic law, not by Torah law

steps.whyThisMatters: This answer sets up the whole next challenge. The question becomes whether a rabbinic separation is really treated more leniently.

phrases.english: Here, it is domains of rabbinic law.
phrases.notes: This is talking about רב דימי's case of passing something through an exempt area.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers a difficulty on the previous amud by limiting רב דימי's case to rabbinic domains.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Limiting the case (אוקימתא): the leniency applies only to רשויות דרבנן.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: It seemed that רב דימי allowed passing through a מקום פטור even where this conflicts with a stricter ruling.
steps.terutzMaskana: רב דימי's ban on exchanging through a מקום פטור applies only to Torah domains. With rabbinic domains, passing through a מקום פטור is allowed.

steps.title: But רבי יוחנן is strict even with rabbinic domains
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא challenges the answer. רבי יוחנן forbids using an in-between area even for רשויות דרבנן, and the גמרא begins quoting the משנה of the wall between two courtyards.
steps.simpleTranslation: But רבי יוחנן said this is forbidden even with rabbinic domains, as we learned: a wall between two courtyards that is ten טפחים high and four wide. The residents make two separate עירובין, and they do not make one shared עירוב.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא attacks the answer it just gave. It begins quoting a משנה that רבי יוחנן commented on, and that משנה will show his strict view.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Carrying between two courtyards without an עירוב is only a rabbinic ban, so the courtyards are רשויות דרבנן. The wall top lies between them like an in-between area. If רבי יוחנן is strict there, then 'rabbinic domains' cannot be the reason to be lenient. The wall's size matters: ten טפחים high and four wide makes it a real separation, so each courtyard needs its own עירוב.

keyTerms.meaning: they make an עירוב (join the residents for carrying)

steps.confusionAlert: Don't look for רבי יוחנן's strict statement inside the quoted משנה. The גמרא is only quoting the משנה here. רבי יוחנן's view comes in Steps 7–8: he rules on a wall less than four טפחים wide, saying each side may bring food up and eat, but the two sides may not exchange.

phrases.english: But surely Rabbi Yochanan
said it even regarding rabbinic domains, as we learned:
phrases.notes: 'Said it' means רבי יוחנן forbade passing an object through an in-between area.

phrases.english: A wall that is between two courtyards,
ten handbreadths high and four wide,
phrases.notes: This size makes the wall a full separation.

phrases.english: they make two eiruvin, but they do not make one.
phrases.notes: Each courtyard counts as a separate domain.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְהָא רַבִּי יוֹחָנָן בָּרְשׁוּיוֹת דְּרַבָּנַן נָמֵי אָמַר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the answer of Step 1.
steps.kashyaTarget: The claim that passing through a מקום פטור is permitted with רשויות דרבנן.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: רבי יוחנן forbids the in-between route even between courtyards, which are only rabbinically separate. So 'rabbinic domains' does not explain the leniency.

steps.title: Fruit on top of the wall
steps.stepSummary: The משנה continues: each courtyard's residents may climb up and eat fruit lying on top of the wall.
steps.simpleTranslation: If there was fruit on top of the wall, these residents may climb up from this side and eat, and those residents may climb up from that side and eat.
steps.whatsHappening: The quoted משנה brings the case at the center of the challenge. Fruit on top of the wall may be eaten by both sides while they stay up on the wall.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In the משנה's case the wall is four טפחים wide, so its top is a place of its own, and each courtyard's residents may climb up and eat there without bringing the fruit down. The גמרא's next move (Step 5) asks about a narrower wall. That narrower case is where רבי יוחנן's view, that each side may use it but not exchange, will appear.
steps.whyThisMatters: This is the clause the challenge depends on. It shows the wall top acting as an in-between space next to two rabbinic domains.

phrases.english: If there was produce on top of it,
these go up from here and eat,
phrases.notes: The residents of one courtyard.

phrases.english: and those go up from there and eat.
phrases.notes: The residents of the other courtyard. They eat on top and do not bring the fruit down.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues the quotation that supports the challenge.
steps.raayaObject: The claim that רבי יוחנן is strict even with רשויות דרבנן.
steps.raayaSupportSource: The משנה of fruit on a wall between two courtyards, which רבי יוחנן will comment on.

steps.title: If the wall is breached
steps.stepSummary: The משנה finishes: a gap of up to ten אמות counts like a doorway, so either one or two עירובין may be made. A larger gap merges the courtyards, so only one עירוב is allowed.
steps.simpleTranslation: If the wall broke open up to ten אמות, they may make two עירובין, or one if they want, because the gap is like a doorway. If it is wider than that, they make one עירוב and may not make two.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא finishes quoting the משנה with its last clause about a broken wall. This part is quoted for completeness and is not the focus of the challenge.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A gap of up to ten אמות is treated like a פתח (doorway). The courtyards keep their separate status but are connected, so either choice works. A gap wider than ten אמות cancels the wall completely, making one courtyard that can only have one עירוב.
steps.whatToRemember: The משנה allows eating fruit on top of a four-טפח-wide wall between two courtyards. The גמרא will next ask about a narrower wall. There, רבי יוחנן's ruling that each side may use it but may not exchange is what challenges the 'rabbinic domains' answer.

phrases.english: If the wall was breached, up to ten cubits,
they may make two eiruvin,
and if they wish, they may make one,
because it is like a doorway.
More than this,
they make one eiruv and do not make two.
phrases.notes: The large gap merges the two courtyards into one domain.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Finishes the quotation of the משנה begun in Step 2.
steps.raayaObject: Completes the quoted source behind the challenge to Step 1.
steps.raayaSupportSource: The last clause of the wall משנה, about a breach.

steps.title: What if the wall is less than four handbreadths wide?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא recalls that the בית מדרש once asked what the law is when the wall from the משנה is less than four טפחים wide.
steps.simpleTranslation: And we discussed this: if the wall is not four handbreadths wide, what is the law?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings up an earlier discussion about the wall from the משנה. It is setting up a disagreement that will show what רבי יוחנן holds.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The משנה let each courtyard eat fruit on top of the wall. That works when the wall is wide enough (four טפחים) to count as a place of its own. The question is what happens when the top is narrower than that.

keyTerms.meaning: And we discussed it, meaning an earlier debate in the בית מדרש
Four טפחים, the minimum width for an area to count as its own place

steps.confusionAlert: This is not a new question the גמרא is asking right now. It is quoting an older discussion to bring out רבי יוחנן's opinion, which supports the קשיא from Step 2.

phrases.english: And we discussed it:
If it is not four handbreadths wide, what is the law?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Uses the wall case from the משנה (Steps 3–4) to ask about a narrower version of it.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: The law for a wall between courtyards whose top is less than four טפחים wide.

steps.title: רב: both courtyards control it, so nothing may be moved
steps.stepSummary: רב rules that the airspace of both courtyards rules over a narrow wall, so nothing may be moved on it, not even a hair's breadth.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב said: The air of two domains controls it, so one may not move anything on it, even a hair's breadth.
steps.whatsHappening: רב answers the question. A narrow wall belongs to both courtyards at once, so it is completely off-limits.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Since the wall top is too small to be its own place, it is swallowed up by both courtyards at the same time. Each courtyard 'pulls' on it, so it ends up forbidden to both. That is why not even the tiniest movement is allowed.

keyTerms.meaning: Controls it, has power over it
Even a hair's breadth, the tiniest amount

phrases.english: Rav said:
The air of two domains controls it,
and one may not move anything on it even a hair's breadth.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַב: אֲוִיר שְׁתֵּי רְשׁוּיוֹת שׁוֹלֶטֶת בּוֹ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question from Step 5.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: A narrow wall is ruled by both courtyards and is completely forbidden.

steps.title: רבי יוחנן: each side may bring food up and eat
steps.stepSummary: רבי יוחנן disagrees and says the residents of each courtyard may bring food up from their own side and eat it on the wall. The implied condition is that the two sides do not swap.
steps.simpleTranslation: And רבי יוחנן said: These may bring up from here and eat, and those may bring up from there and eat.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי יוחנן gives a more lenient answer. Each courtyard may use the narrow wall top, but each only from its own side.
steps.deeperAnalysis: To רבי יוחנן, a spot smaller than four by four is an exempt area (מקום פטור) that either side may use. The wording 'these from here, those from here' hints at a limit: the two sides may not pass things to each other across it. That limit is the key point for the קשיא.

keyTerms.meaning: From here, from their own side

phrases.english: And Rabbi Yoḥanan said:
These bring up food from here and eat,
and those bring up food from here and eat.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְרַבִּי יוֹחָנָן אָמַר: אֵלּוּ מַעֲלִין מִכָּאן וְאוֹכְלִין
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives a competing answer to רב's answer in Step 6.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: Each courtyard may use the narrow wall from its own side, without exchanging with the other side.

steps.title: רבי יוחנן is consistent: no swapping through an exempt spot
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא shows that רבי יוחנן follows his usual view. רב דימי reported that רבי יוחנן allows people from רשות הרבים and רשות היחיד to use a small exempt spot, but only if they do not swap things. So רבי יוחנן forbids swapping even between domains that are separate only מדרבנן, which seems to undo the answer from Step 1.
steps.simpleTranslation: And רבי יוחנן follows his own reasoning. When רב דימי came, he said that רבי יוחנן said: A place less than four by four may be used by people of the public domain and people of the private domain to load burdens onto their shoulders, as long as they do not exchange!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא backs up the challenge. It shows רבי יוחנן consistently forbids passing things between two domains through an in-between spot, even in the courtyard case where the separation is only מדרבנן.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Two rulings of רבי יוחנן share the same rule: an exempt spot may be used by each side, but not for exchange. In the wall case, both courtyards are only rabbinically separate, and he still forbids exchange. This contradicts Step 1's claim that רב דימי's leniency works because the domains are only rabbinic. The problem is sharper because רב דימי himself reported רבי יוחנן's no-exchange rule (stated about רשות הרבים and רשות היחיד), and the גמרא links that rule to רבי יוחנן's strict wall ruling.

keyTerms.meaning: He follows his own reasoning, is consistent
When רב דימי came from ארץ ישראל to Bavel
To load a burden onto the shoulder
As long as they do not exchange with each other

steps.whyThisMatters: This sets the rule of the מקום פטור: each side may use it alone, but it cannot serve as a bridge between two domains.

phrases.english: And Rabbi Yoḥanan follows his own reasoning,
for when Rav Dimi came
he said that Rabbi Yoḥanan said:

phrases.aramaic: מָקוֹם שֶׁאֵין בּוֹ אַרְבָּעָה עַל אַרְבָּעָה —
phrases.english: A place that is not four by four handbreadths —
it is permitted for the people of the public domain
and for the people of the private domain to load burdens on it,
as long as they do not exchange!

steps.triggerLanguage: וְאַזְדָּא רַבִּי יוֹחָנָן לְטַעְמֵיהּ, דְּכִי אֲתָא רַב דִּימִי אָמַר רַבִּי יוֹחָנָן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Links רבי יוחנן's wall ruling in Step 7 to his ruling about a small exempt spot, completing the challenge begun in Step 2.
steps.raayaObject: That רבי יוחנן forbids exchange through an in-between spot, even between domains that are only rabbinically separate.
steps.raayaSupportSource: רב דימי's report of רבי יוחנן's ruling about a spot smaller than four by four between רשות הרבים and רשות היחיד.
steps.kashyaTarget: The answer in Step 1 that רב דימי's leniency deals with domains separate only מדרבנן.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: רבי יוחנן forbids exchange even in a rabbinic case, and רב דימי himself transmitted this, so רב דימי's leniency cannot be explained that way.

steps.title: The wall ruling was reported by זעירי, not רב דימי
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא answers that רבי יוחנן's ruling about the wall was transmitted by זעירי. רב דימי had a different tradition of רבי יוחנן, so there is no contradiction for him.
steps.simpleTranslation: That ruling, זעירי said it.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the challenge by saying different students reported different traditions from רבי יוחנן. The strict wall ruling came from זעירי, not רב דימי.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The strictness in the rabbinic wall case is זעירי's version of רבי יוחנן. רב דימי's version allows exchange where the domains are only rabbinically separate, and forbids it only where Torah domains are involved, as in the רשות הרבים case. So the Step 1 answer holds for רב דימי.

keyTerms.meaning: זעירי, an אמורא who transmitted teachings

phrases.english: That ruling, Ze'eiri said it.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge of Steps 2 and 8.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Different transmitters (אמוראים) report different traditions of the same teacher.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: We thought רב דימי himself held that רבי יוחנן forbids exchange even in rabbinic domains.
steps.terutzMaskana: The strict wall ruling is זעירי's tradition. רב דימי's tradition allows it in rabbinic domains.

steps.title: But for זעירי, the earlier case is still a problem
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא notes that even though רב דימי is now fine, זעירי's version of רבי יוחנן still conflicts with the earlier lenient ruling (the water channel between two windows).
steps.simpleTranslation: And according to זעירי, this is difficult!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא points out that the answer only moves the problem. זעירי, who reports the strict view, now has trouble with the earlier lenient case.
steps.deeperAnalysis: זעירי's רבי יוחנן forbids exchange even between rabbinic domains. The earlier ruling about the channel between two windows allowed it. So according to זעירי, that earlier ruling is hard to explain, and the difficulty stands.
steps.whatToRemember: רב: a wall less than four טפחים wide is forbidden to both courtyards. רבי יוחנן: each side may use it but not exchange. The strict version of רבי יוחנן in rabbinic domains is זעירי's tradition, and it leaves the earlier lenient case difficult for זעירי.

phrases.english: And according to Ze'eiri, this is difficult!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Raises a new difficulty that follows from the answer in Step 9.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: If רבי יוחנן forbids exchange even between rabbinic domains, the earlier lenient ruling about the water channel between two windows conflicts with זעירי's version.

steps.title: זעירי reads the water-channel ruling as being about the channel's own width
steps.stepSummary: זעירי explains that the measurements in the water-channel ruling refer to the width of the channel itself. He also holds that רב דימי's rule, that a כרמלית must be at least four טפחים wide, is a matter the תנאים argue about.
steps.simpleTranslation: זעירי explains that the ruling is about the water channel itself. And רב דימי's rule is actually a dispute between תנאים.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the problem from Step 10 by showing how זעירי understands the lenient water-channel ruling. Once it is read his way, it no longer clashes with his version of רבי יוחנן.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Step 10 asked how זעירי's רבי יוחנן, who forbids swapping, could fit with the lenient water-channel ruling. זעירי answers that the measurements in that ruling describe how wide the channel itself is. When the channel is too narrow, it is not a כרמלית at all, so the leniency was never permission to swap between domains. This only works if the minimum size of a כרמלית is debated, so זעירי says רב דימי's four-טפחים rule is not agreed by everyone and is really a dispute between תנאים.

keyTerms.meaning: Explains it as referring to (sets the case in a specific way)
It is a dispute between תנאים

steps.confusionAlert: זעירי is not saying the narrow channel is a כרמלית that you are allowed to swap with. He is saying a channel that narrow is not a כרמלית at all.

phrases.english: Ze'eiri explains it (the ruling)
phrases.notes: זעירי sets up how the water-channel ruling should be read.

phrases.english: as referring to the water channel itself.
phrases.notes: The measurements describe the width of the channel itself, which decides whether it counts as a כרמלית.

phrases.english: And Rav Dimi's teaching is a dispute between tanna'im.
phrases.notes: The rule that a כרמלית needs four טפחים is not agreed by all the תנאים.

steps.triggerLanguage: זְעֵירִי מוֹקֵים לַהּ בְּאַמַּת הַמַּיִם גּוּפַהּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge from Step 10 against זעירי's version of רבי יוחנן.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Re-reading the case: the source is about the channel's own size, not about permission to swap.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: We thought the lenient water-channel ruling allowed swapping between rabbinic domains, which would clash with זעירי's רבי יוחנן.
steps.terutzMaskana: The leniency exists because a narrow channel is not a כרמלית at all. The four-טפחים minimum is a dispute between תנאים.

steps.title: Shouldn't the narrow channel count as a 'hole' of the larger כרמלית?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא challenges זעירי's answer. Even if the channel inside the courtyard is too narrow to be a כרמלית by itself, it should still count as one of the 'holes' (חורין) of the bigger channel outside, which is a כרמלית.
steps.simpleTranslation: But let it be treated like the holes of a כרמלית!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא pushes back on Step 11. It asks why the narrow channel doesn't take on the status of the big כרמלית it connects to.
steps.deeperAnalysis: There is a known rule for רשות היחיד: small holes in its walls are treated as part of it, even if they are too small to be a domain on their own. The גמרא suggests the same logic for a כרמלית. If that is right, the narrow channel would be a כרמלית after all, and the problem from Step 10 would come back.

keyTerms.meaning: An in-between domain that the חכמים created, neither fully private nor fully public

phrases.english: But let it be like the holes of a karmelit!
phrases.notes: The narrow channel would get the status of the bigger כרמלית it is attached to.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the answer given in Step 11.
steps.kashyaTarget: זעירי's claim that the narrow channel is not a כרמלית.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Holes attached to a domain take on that domain's status. So the narrow channel should count as part of the large כרמלית anyway.

steps.title: A כרמלית has no 'holes'
steps.stepSummary: אביי בר אבין and רב חנינא בר אבין both say that the 'holes' rule does not apply to a כרמלית at all.
steps.simpleTranslation: אביי בר אבין and רב חנינא בר אבין both said: a כרמלית has no holes.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the challenge from Step 12. It denies that the 'holes' rule applies to a כרמלית at all.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A כרמלית exists only because the חכמים created it, so its rules are not made as strict as those of a full Torah-level domain. That is why it does not absorb small attached spaces the way רשות היחיד does. So the narrow channel stays outside the כרמלית, and זעירי's answer holds.

keyTerms.meaning: A כרמלית has no 'holes' (it does not absorb attached small spaces)

phrases.aramaic: אַבָּיֵי בַּר אָבִין וְרַב חֲנִינָא בַּר אָבִין
phrases.english: Abaye bar Avin and Rav Ḥanina bar Avin
phrases.notes: Two brothers who say the same thing.

phrases.english: who both said:
There are no holes for a karmelit.
phrases.notes: The 'holes' rule does not extend to a domain the חכמים created.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge from Step 12.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Denying the premise: the 'holes' rule does not apply to a כרמלית.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Small holes are absorbed into a כרמלית just as they are into רשות היחיד.
steps.terutzMaskana: A כרמלית does not absorb holes, so the narrow channel is not a כרמלית.

steps.title: Holes count only when they are right next to the כרמלית
steps.stepSummary: רב אשי gives a second answer. Even if a כרמלית can have holes, that is only true for holes right next to it. The channel in the courtyard is far away from the כרמלית.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב אשי said: You can even say that a כרמלית has holes. But that is only when the hole is right next to it. Here, the channel is far away.
steps.whatsHappening: רב אשי gives a different answer to the challenge from Step 12. He does not deny the 'holes' rule. Instead he limits it.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רב אשי accepts that a כרמלית can absorb holes. But a hole is treated as part of the כרמלית only when it sits right beside it and gets swallowed up by it. The channel running through the courtyard is far from the big channel in the street, so it does not take on its status. Either way, זעירי's answer still stands.
steps.whatToRemember: זעירי's version of רבי יוחנן survives. The water-channel leniency exists because a narrow channel is not a כרמלית at all. It does not become one through the 'holes' rule, either because a כרמלית has no holes (אביי בר אבין and רב חנינא בר אבין) or because this channel is too far away (רב אשי).

phrases.english: Rav Ashi said:
You can even say there are holes for a karmelit —
phrases.notes: Now he goes along with the opposite idea from step 13.

phrases.english: this applies only when it is adjacent.
phrases.notes: A hole right next to the כרמלית is swallowed up by it.

phrases.english: Here, it is far removed.
phrases.notes: The channel in the courtyard is far from the כרמלית in the street.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: A second answer to the challenge from Step 12. It works even if the premise rejected in Step 13 is true.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Limiting the rule by distance: holes count only when they are right next to the כרמלית.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: If a כרמלית has holes, any attached channel would become part of it.
steps.terutzMaskana: Only holes right next to the כרמלית are absorbed. This channel is far away, so it is not a כרמלית.

steps.title: רבינא: The measurements refer to openings in the partitions
steps.stepSummary: רבינא answers the difficulty differently. The three and four טפחים in the water-channel ruling do not measure the channel or its banks. They measure openings made in the partitions at the ends of the channel so the water can flow through.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבינא said: The case is one where he made outlets for it at its mouth.
steps.whatsHappening: רבינא gives a brand-new way to read the water-channel ruling. The numbers describe the size of the gaps cut into the partitions where the water enters and exits.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The earlier answers struggled because they treated the numbers as widths of a space, which raised questions about כרמלית and its 'holes.' רבינא moves the numbers onto the partition openings. Once that is done, the whole כרמלית question no longer comes up.

keyTerms.meaning: Outlets, meaning gaps or openings that let the water pass through
At its mouth, meaning the ends of the channel where water enters and leaves
For example, or 'the case is where.' It introduces how to picture the case

phrases.english: Ravina said:
For example, where he made for it
phrases.notes: 'It' is the water channel.

phrases.english: outlets at its mouth.
phrases.notes: These are openings in the partitions at the channel's ends.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: This is an alternative to זעירי's reading in Step 11 of the water-channel ברייתא's three and four טפחים. רבינא reads the measurements as outlets in the partitions, not as the width of the channel.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Redefining the case: the measurements refer to something else entirely
steps.terutzHavaAmina: We assumed the three and four טפחים measured the width of a space (the channel or its banks). That created the כרמלית and 'holes' problem.
steps.terutzMaskana: The measurements are the size of gaps in the partitions, so no כרמלית question arises at all.

steps.title: Each side follows its known view on לבוד
steps.stepSummary: With רבינא's reading, the dispute fits neatly. The רבנן hold that a gap counts as closed (לבוד) only if it is under three טפחים. רבן שמעון בן גמליאל holds that a gap under four טפחים also counts as closed.
steps.simpleTranslation: The רבנן follow their own reasoning, and רבן שמעון בן גמליאל follows his own reasoning.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא shows why רבינא's answer works. The argument over three versus four טפחים is just the famous argument about how big a gap can be and still be treated as closed.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Under לבוד, a small enough gap is viewed as if it were sealed. For the רבנן the limit is under three טפחים, and for רבן שמעון בן גמליאל it is under four. So an outlet smaller than the limit leaves the partition whole, and drawing water is allowed. This closes the water-channel discussion.

keyTerms.meaning: They go according to their own reasoning, meaning they stay consistent with their known view
The rule that a small gap is treated as closed
A תנא who holds that לבוד works for gaps under four טפחים

steps.whatToRemember: According to רבינא, the three and four טפחים in the water-channel ruling are the sizes of openings in the partitions. The dispute is the well-known argument about לבוד: under three for the רבנן, under four for רבן שמעון בן גמליאל.
steps.confusionAlert: Do not mix this up with the earlier answers. Here the numbers are not the width of the channel or its banks. They are the gaps in the walls.

phrases.english: And the Rabbis follow their reasoning,
phrases.notes: לבוד applies only to a gap of less than three טפחים.

phrases.english: and Rabban Shimon ben Gamliel follows his reasoning.
phrases.notes: לבוד applies to a gap of less than four טפחים.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: This finishes רבינא's answer by linking the dispute to the known argument about לבוד.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: According to רבינא, the water-channel dispute between the רבנן and רבן שמעון בן גמליאל is their known לבוד dispute applied to outlets in the partitions. It is not a dispute about the minimum size of a כרמלית.

steps.title: משנה: A balcony over water needs a ten-טפח partition
steps.stepSummary: A new משנה begins. On שבת you may not draw water through a hole in a balcony that sticks out over water, unless a partition ten טפחים high is built around the hole. The partition may be above the balcony or hanging below it.
steps.simpleTranslation: With a balcony that is above the water, you may not draw water from it on שבת unless a partition ten טפחים high was made for it, whether above or below.
steps.whatsHappening: A new משנה opens with a new case: a balcony over a river or sea. It teaches what you need in order to draw water through a hole in the balcony floor on שבת.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The water underneath is a כרמלית. Pulling a bucket up from it into the balcony would move something from one domain into another. A ten-טפח partition around the hole marks off the water below as part of the balcony's private area. The partition may stand on top of the balcony around the hole, or hang down beneath it, because a partition is viewed as reaching down to the water.

keyTerms.meaning: The משנה, here starting a new section
A balcony that sticks out from a building
Draw water, as when filling a bucket
Ten handbreadths, the standard height of a halachic partition

steps.whyThisMatters: This uses the idea that a partition can be seen as extending down to the water. That idea is discussed later in the גמרא.

phrases.english: MISHNA
A balcony that is above the water
phrases.notes: It extends out over a river or sea.

phrases.english: one may not draw water from it on Shabbat
phrases.notes: This means through a hole in its floor.

phrases.aramaic: אֶלָּא אִם כֵּן עָשׂוּ לָהּ מְחִיצָה
phrases.english: unless they made a partition for it
ten handbreadths high,
whether above or below.
phrases.notes: The partition may be on top of the balcony or hanging beneath it.

steps.triggerLanguage: מַתְנִי׳ גְּזוּזְטְרָא שֶׁהִיא לְמַעְלָה מִן הַמַּיִם
steps.relationToPreviousStep: This starts a new משנה. It continues the theme of drawing water on שבת from a channel or a body of water.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Drawing water through a hole in a balcony over water on שבת requires a ten-טפח partition around the hole, either above or below the balcony.

steps.title: משנה: Two balconies, one above the other
steps.stepSummary: Suppose two balconies are stacked one above the other, and only the upper one built a partition. Then the residents of both are forbidden to draw water until they make an עירוב between them.
steps.simpleTranslation: Likewise, with two balconies one above the other: if they made a partition for the upper one and not for the lower one, both are forbidden until they make an עירוב.
steps.whatsHappening: The משנה adds a second case. Two balconies share the space enclosed by one partition, and they need an עירוב to use it.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The upper balcony's partition creates one enclosed area over the water. The lower balcony also has access to that area. Since two separate households now share it, neither may draw water until they join together with an עירוב.

keyTerms.meaning: The upper one, here the upper balcony
The lower one, here the lower balcony
That they make an עירוב, joining their properties so they may share the space

steps.confusionAlert: Notice that the upper balcony is also forbidden, even though it built the partition itself. The lower balcony's shared access is what causes the problem for both.

phrases.english: And likewise, two balconies
one above the other,
if they made a partition for the upper one
and did not make one for the lower one —
both are forbidden
until they make an eiruv.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְכֵן שְׁתֵּי גְזוּזְטְרָאוֹת זוֹ לְמַעְלָה מִזּוֹ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: This continues the משנה by applying the balcony rule to two balconies that share one partition.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: If only the upper balcony has a partition, both balconies may not draw water until they make an עירוב together.

steps.title: Our משנה does not follow חנניא בן עקביא
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא states that our משנה, which requires a ten-טפחים partition, disagrees with חנניא בן עקביא. He allows drawing water through a 4-by-4 טפחים hole cut into a balcony of 4-by-4 אמות, with no extra partition.
steps.simpleTranslation: גמרא: Our משנה is not like חנניא בן עקביא. A ברייתא teaches that חנניא בן עקביא says: If a balcony is four אמות by four אמות, a person may cut a hole of four טפחים by four טפחים in it and draw water through it.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא begins by pointing out that a תנא, חנניא בן עקביא, disagrees with our משנה. It proves this from a ברייתא.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Our משנה said you need a ten-טפחים partition around the hole. חנניא בן עקביא says that if the balcony is large and the hole is 4-by-4, no extra partition is needed. The balcony floor around the hole is viewed as if it bends down and stretches into a ten-טפחים partition (כוף וגוד).

keyTerms.meaning: A balcony jutting out over water
He carves or cuts out (a hole)
'Stretch the partition down': we imagine the edge extending downward as a wall

steps.confusionAlert: Watch the units. The balcony is measured in אמות (4 by 4 אמות), but the hole is measured in טפחים (4 by 4 טפחים).

phrases.english: Gemara
Our Mishnah is not in accordance with Chananya ben Akavya.
As it was taught: Chananya ben Akavya says:

phrases.aramaic: גְּזוּזְטְרָא שֶׁיֵּשׁ בָּהּ אַרְבַּע עַל אַרְבַּע אַמּוֹת
phrases.english: A balcony that has in it four by four cubits
one carves out in it (a hole of) four by four (handbreadths)
and draws water.
phrases.notes: No additional partition is required.

steps.triggerLanguage: מַתְנִיתִין דְּלָא כַּחֲנַנְיָא בֶּן עֲקַבְיָא. דְּתַנְיָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Begins the גמרא on the balcony משנה from steps 17-18 by identifying a dissenting תנא.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: According to חנניא בן עקביא, a 4x4-אמות balcony with a 4x4-טפחים hole needs no extra partition to draw water on שבת. Our משנה disagrees.

steps.title: The leniency applies only to ים טבריא
steps.stepSummary: רבי יוחנן, quoting רבי יוסי בן זימרא, limits חנניא בן עקביא's leniency to the Sea of טבריא. That lake has clear banks and is surrounded by towns and enclosures. Other bodies of water do not get the leniency.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי יוחנן said in the name of רבי יוסי בן זימרא: רבי חנניא בן עקביא allowed this only at the Sea of טבריא. That is because it has banks, and towns and enclosures surround it. But for other waters, he did not allow it.
steps.whatsHappening: An אמורא narrows the leniency we just saw. It only works at the Sea of טבריא.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Usually, imagined partitions made by the hole's edges are not enough. The Sea of טבריא, however, is enclosed by visible banks and surrounding towns, so it feels like part of a settled, enclosed area. That added factor is what makes the weak partition acceptable. A large open sea lacks it.

keyTerms.meaning: Banks or edges of a body of water

steps.whyThisMatters: It shows that חנניא בן עקביא's leniency is not a general rule. It depends on the special setting of טבריא, and this sets up the next ברייתא about his rulings for the people of טבריא.

phrases.aramaic: אָמַר רַבִּי יוֹחָנָן מִשּׁוּם רַבִּי יוֹסֵי בֶּן זִימְרָא:
phrases.english: Rabbi Yochanan said in the name of Rabbi Yosei ben Zimra:

phrases.aramaic: לֹא הִתִּיר רַבִּי חֲנַנְיָא בֶּן עֲקַבְיָא
phrases.english: Rabbi Chananya ben Akavya did not permit
except at the Sea of Tiberias,
since it has banks,
and towns and enclosures surround it,
but with other waters, no.

steps.triggerLanguage: לֹא הִתִּיר רַבִּי חֲנַנְיָא בֶּן עֲקַבְיָא אֶלָּא בְּיַמָּהּ שֶׁל טְבֶרְיָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Limits the scope of the opinion quoted in step 19.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: חנניא בן עקביא's balcony leniency applies only to the Sea of טבריא, because it is enclosed by banks, towns, and enclosures.

steps.title: Three leniencies for the people of טבריא
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא lists three things חנניא בן עקביא allowed the people of טבריא: drawing water through a balcony on שבת, storing produce in pods, and drying off with a towel.
steps.simpleTranslation: The רבנן taught: רבי חנניא בן עקביא allowed three things to the people of טבריא. They may draw water from a balcony on שבת. They may store produce in pods. They may dry themselves with a towel.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a ברייתא with a list of three leniencies. The next steps will explain each item.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This ברייתא confirms what רבי יוחנן said: the balcony leniency was given specifically to the people of טבריא. It also adds two more leniencies whose meaning is not yet clear. The גמרא will go through them one at a time.

phrases.english: Our Sages taught:

phrases.aramaic: שְׁלֹשָׁה דְּבָרִים הִתִּיר רַבִּי חֲנַנְיָא בֶּן עֲקַבְיָא
phrases.english: Rabbi Chananya ben Akavya permitted three things
to the people of Tiberias:
they may draw water from a balcony on Shabbat,
and they may store (produce) in pods,
and they may dry themselves with a towel.

steps.triggerLanguage: שְׁלֹשָׁה דְּבָרִים הִתִּיר רַבִּי חֲנַנְיָא בֶּן עֲקַבְיָא לְאַנְשֵׁי טְבֶרְיָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Brings a ברייתא that places the balcony leniency within a list of rulings specifically for טבריא.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: חנניא בן עקביא gave the people of טבריא three leniencies: drawing water through a balcony, storing in pods, and drying with a towel.

steps.title: The first item is the balcony case already discussed
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא explains that the first leniency, drawing water from a balcony, is the case discussed above.
steps.simpleTranslation: 'They may draw water from a balcony on שבת': this is what we already said.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא starts explaining the list. It says the first item needs no new explanation.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Nothing new is added here. The first item simply points back to the balcony with the 4-by-4 hole from steps 19-20, which was allowed only at טבריא.

phrases.english: 'They may draw water from a balcony on Shabbat':
this is what we said.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Begins explaining the three items in the ברייתא of step 21.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The balcony leniency is the 4x4 hole ruling already explained.

steps.title: What does storing in pods mean?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks what the second leniency, טומנין בעצה, refers to.
steps.simpleTranslation: 'And they may store in pods': what is this?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks for the meaning of the second item. This sets up the answer in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Unlike the first item, this one has not been discussed yet. The גמרא needs to explain which law it refers to and what exactly חנניא בן עקביא permitted.

keyTerms.meaning: What is it? (asks for an explanation)

steps.confusionAlert: Here טומנין does not mean wrapping hot food to keep it warm for שבת. It means storing produce in pods or straw. As the next step shows, the issue is about ritual purity.

phrases.english: 'And they may store in pods':
what is it?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves from the first item to the second item in the list.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Which law is meant by 'storing in pods,' and what was permitted?

steps.title: A ברייתא about collecting residue with dew on it
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא answers by quoting a ברייתא. If someone gets up early to bring in plant residue because it still has dew on it, the produce stored in it falls under כי יותן, meaning it becomes able to become impure.
steps.simpleTranslation: As a ברייתא teaches: If someone got up early to bring in residue, and he did it because the residue still has dew on it, this counts as 'כי יותן' ('if water be put').
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא begins its answer by quoting a ברייתא about dew and ritual impurity. The ברייתא continues in the next part of the text.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Food can only become טמא after it gets wet in a way its owner wants (כי יותן). If the person chose the early hour because he wanted the dew-covered residue, he wants the moisture, so the produce stored in it can now become טמא. The link to חנניא בן עקביא's leniency will come as the ברייתא continues.

keyTerms.meaning: 'If water be put' (ויקרא יא:לח): food becomes able to become impure after getting wet with the owner's approval
Making food able to become טמא through contact with liquid

steps.whyThisMatters: It shows that 'storing in pods' is a question of ritual purity, not a שבת law. The point is whether the dew on the pods makes the stored produce able to become טמא.

phrases.english: As it was taught:
If one rose early to bring residue,
if (he did so) because there is dew on it,
it is in the category of 'if water be put',
phrases.notes: The ברייתא continues next.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of step 23 by quoting the relevant ברייתא.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: 'Storing in pods' refers to the law of כי יותן. Bringing in dew-covered residue on purpose makes the produce stored in it able to become טמא.

steps.title: Bringing in the residue only to save work time does not count
steps.stepSummary: The ברייתא finishes its rule. If a person brought in the residue early only so he would not lose time from his work, and not because he wanted the dew, the produce does not fall under כי יותן.
steps.simpleTranslation: But if he got up early only so that he would not lose time from his work, it is not under 'כי יותן' (the produce does not become able to become impure).
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא finishes its rule by giving the opposite case. If the person did not care about the dew and only wanted to save work time, the wet residue does not make the stored produce able to become impure.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Under the rule of כי יותן, a liquid only makes food able to become impure if the owner wanted that liquid. In step 24, the person wanted the dew, so it counted. Here he only wanted to get his work done, so the dew is just there by accident and does not count. This is what makes it possible to store produce in the residue without worry.

keyTerms.meaning: So that he will not be idle (not lose time)
'If water is put' (ויקרא י״א:ל״ח). This is the rule that a liquid the owner wanted makes food able to become impure.
It is not included in (the rule)

steps.confusionAlert: The dew is just as wet in both cases. The only difference is what the person wanted. The physical wetness alone does not decide whether the food can become impure. The person's intention decides it.
steps.whyThisMatters: This contrast sets up the unspecified case on the next amud. That is where חנניא בן עקביא's leniency for storing in residue will come out.

phrases.english: But if it was for the sake of (the reason)
phrases.notes: Now comes the other side, compared to the case in step 24, where he wanted the dew.

phrases.english: that he not be idle from his work
phrases.notes: He got up early only to save time, not because he wanted the dew.

phrases.english: it is not under 'if it be put' (the produce does not become able to become impure)
phrases.notes: Dew he did not want does not count.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Finishes the ברייתא quoted in step 24 by giving the opposite case (he did not want the dew).
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: Produce stored in residue is not able to become impure when the residue was brought in only to save work time, because the dew was not wanted.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: What does טומנין בעצה mean? (asked in step 23)

steps.title: Turning to the unspecified case
steps.stepSummary: The word וּסְתָם ('and ordinarily') begins the ברייתא's ruling for a case where the person did not say why he brought the residue early. The sentence continues on the next amud.
steps.simpleTranslation: And in the ordinary case, when he did not say why...
steps.whatsHappening: This one word is a setup line. The ברייתא is getting ready to rule on the unspecified case, where the person did not say why he came early. The sentence continues on the next amud.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Two cases have now been set up: wanting the dew, and only wanting to save work time. The ברייתא now turns to the unspecified case, where the person never said why he came early. The ruling on that case, and חנניא בן עקביא's view of it, comes on the next amud.

keyTerms.meaning: And ordinarily; in the usual case, when nothing specific is said

phrases.english: And ordinarily
phrases.notes: The sentence continues on the next amud. It rules on a case where the person did not state his reason.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues the ברייתא from steps 24–25 by turning to the unspecified case, where the person did not say why he brought the residue early.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: Not yet complete. This opens the application that will finish answering step 23's question about טומנין בעצה.
